question: Why put `dispatch` in its own context?
options: `dispatch` cannot be stored together with state
Its identity never changes, so dispatch-only consumers avoid re-rendering on state changes
React requires one context per Hook
It makes the reducer run faster
explanation: Consumers re-render when their context value changes. Isolating the stable `dispatch` lets components that only send actions skip state updates.

question: Why create the contexts with `null` as the default?
options: So the custom Hooks can detect a missing provider and throw a clear error
explanation: A `null` default signals that no provider exists above. The Hook turns that into an explicit error instead of a confusing crash later.
